title: Market-intelligence lenses
tagline: A complete, self-updating graph of NYC AI rooms and the market around them, read through four lenses: attended, research, market and job.
phase: Pivot: from fixed lanes to a discovery loop over a complete graph
why: It started with a silent failure: from 8 August, topic trends stopped absorbing new topics. On 10 November an audit of the live graph found a wider gap. Only 30 of 85 attended events carry first-hand claims (12 of the 61 from April to July), and 45 of 97 researched events never reached the graph. The graph's first claim was written on 18 September, so anything earlier exists only where a later backfill brought it in. The cause: graph writes were the last step of long manual commands. They were mandatory on paper, but nothing enforced or measured them. The market side was also too small. It polled a fixed list of 40 companies, and one source test was scoped as matching a paid vendor instead of discovering anything new.
mission: Make the graph complete backwards and self-maintaining forwards. Data arrives through 'lanes': scheduled jobs that each feed one kind of signal (hiring, company news, research papers, feeds). A nightly reconciler compares every source (event folders, transcripts, research briefs, Notion) against the graph and fills the gaps through one guarded writer. On top of that runs a discovery loop. The themes rising in the graph and each week's events pick what to search for. Read-only agents search the market. New companies join the watchlist when the evidence supports it. Claims heard in the room are checked against what the web says. Every reuse of a fact is counted.
destination: Every event since April is in the graph with its research, roster and first-hand claims. Every source has a completeness score and an alarm. Before any room, the brief says what moved in that room's themes this week, which companies are new, and where what speakers said agrees or conflicts with the market. The Monday Market Brief is the weekly proof.
showcase: Auditing a knowledge graph against its own sources and stating each gap as a dated count before proposing a fix
Reconciliation over reminders: a nightly job checks what should exist and fills the gap, instead of hoping each manual step ran (the pattern Kubernetes uses)
A discovery loop: the graph's own trends generate the search questions, read-only agents fetch, and one guarded writer stores the results
Keeping facts honest over time: each new claim is marked as corroborating, refining, replacing or contradicting older ones, and only real conflicts go to a human
The operating rule each lane is held to: a run log, an alarm, a reader and a kill rule. The audit found two lanes breaking it, and fixing them is part of this phase

metrics.note: akta is the paid company-signals trial used as the reference. With dates shifted by 10 days, the null is 0.06–0.13 for the free stack and 0.07–0.18 for the free stack plus Clay. A blinded model labelled the signals; Alex's 20-label spot check agreed on 17 of 20 (first-party, 2026-11-08). Since 10 November this is one input, not the goal. 'Free stack' means news sources that cost nothing. 'Null' is the score from matching on shuffled dates, the luck baseline.

decisions.decision: Build four lenses with sliceable cohorts instead of one trend view.
decisions.why: Thin data is a reason to ingest more, not to shrink the scope.

decisions.decision: Lane 2 runs on the free stack plus Clay.
decisions.why: It was the only measured option that cleared the recall and coverage floors (0.69 and 0.88).

decisions.decision: Replace list-polling with a discovery loop: rising themes, coverage gaps and each week's events generate the searches, and the watchlist grows on evidence.
decisions.why: Matching a vendor on a fixed list defends coverage that already exists. A read-only pilot found that 34 of 38 companies driving the three fastest-rising themes were missing from the graph.

decisions.decision: Scheduled jobs run the loop. Findings are held in a staging table first, and they're promoted into the graph unattended only after a precision spot-check clears 0.8. The watchlist grows itself, and only contradictions reach Alex.
decisions.why: Anything that depended on a manual trigger has died in this project before. The one gate kept up front is a quality floor on web-derived claims.

decisions.decision: Make the graph complete backwards and self-maintaining forwards, with a completeness score per source.
decisions.why: The audit showed the write steps exist but are skipped silently, so the fix is a reconciler that checks, not a reminder.

open.question: How should events that were researched but not attended be stored? Recommended: a 'researched' event type, promoted to attended on evidence.
How is attendance confirmed? Recommended: keep the evidence rule, with a weekly tick list from the reconciler.
What is the completeness backstop? Recommended: a nightly reconciler rather than blocking hooks or a weekly checklist.
How are private sources handled? Recommended: claims only, opt-in per item, the source text never stored.
Register the always-on machine as the scheduled-run environment (a five-minute setup on that machine).

risks.risk: Scheduled runs currently live on a laptop. When it sleeps, the loop goes quiet, which is the failure the design exists to prevent.
risks.mitigation: Move them to the always-on machine. Today's health check flags a lane after 7 quiet days and fails it after 14. Phase 1 tightens daily lanes to flag after 2 and fail after 4.

risks.risk: Two lanes have run on schedule for weeks while writing nothing, and the health check didn't count it.
risks.mitigation: Start their writes or retire them on purpose. Phase 1 makes the health check count a run that writes nothing as a failure.

risks.risk: Web searches lean on news aggregators, so dates and figures can be wrong.
risks.mitigation: Fetch the original page for every item before it is written, and spot-check precision against a floor of 0.8 before the loop runs unattended.

risks.risk: The backfill is large, and entity duplicates can multiply across sources.
risks.mitigation: Dry-run every batch first, map alternate names to one company, and write everything through the one guarded writer.

log.text: Decisions: discovery loop, scheduled routines as the runner, staged writes, autonomous watchlist. Phase 1 is planned to ship this week.
Pilot theme search: 68 dated events and 38 companies across three rising themes, 34 of them new to the graph.
Graph audit: 30 of 85 attended events with first-hand claims, 52 of 97 researched events in the graph, first claim written 18 September.
Decision: lane 2 runs on the free stack plus Clay. The build has started.
Lane 2 bake-off: the free stack plus Clay reached 0.69 recall against akta (floor 0.60) and 0.88 coverage.
Lanes 0 and 3 merged. Lane 4's table and fetcher passed review.
Backlog topics assigned to themes and three themes added.
Gap diagnosed on the live graph and the fix plan written.
